Hi all,

Thanks for the context. Quick legal read attached (Redline_Summary_Maya_Karthik_20261008.pdf). Bottom-line recommendations:

1) Subprocessor approval: we can agree to a notification-plus-approval process, but request a "reasonableness" clause: Redwood to approve unless material non-compliance is shown within 15 business days. This avoids blocking transient vendors.

2) Data residency: we cannot broadly accept uncontrolled cross-border processing for EU-covered data. Propose: carveout language that allows the backup vendor to process only if (a) customer has explicitly consented or (b) data is pseudonymized and encrypted with keys stored in the customer's region.

3) Audit rights / evidence: we will provide SOC2 attachments and an evidence matrix. We will not agree to unfettered on-site audits of Redwood's vendors; propose scoped right to receive SOC2 Type II and encrypted-storage attestations plus a third-party assessor summary. For anything beyond that, we require a written incident-based scope and Redwood's legal approval.

4) Encryption & key management: add explicit flow-down requiring encryption at rest and in transit; where customer-specific keys are required (KMS/HSM), we can include an option in the Order Form addendum.

5) Order Form change mechanics: suggest we use an Order Form addendum with a short clause referencing the DPA rather than amending the MSA broadly. This keeps the change scoped to affected accounts.

I've attached a redline summary and an evidence matrix template (also attached in XLS) for Ops to fill. Marissa, can you prepare a short cover memo and mark any items requiring Commercial or Leadership sign-off? Priyom, if this ends up impacting pricing or credits for restricted regions, please flag.

I'll aim to finalize legal language by COB 2026-10-08, pending Ops evidence.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redline_Summary_Maya_Karthik_20261008.pdf; Evidence_Matrix_S3-SOC2.xlsx
